profile.headline: R&D Software Engineer at Keysight Technologies
profile.summary:
Specialties: Programming languages: C/C++, some Java. Fortran and a smattering of assemblers from way back.
GUI: Qt, some Mac (Carbon).
Scripting: Perl, Python, learning Ruby, various shells (bash, csh, etc).
Tools: CVS/bugzilla/bonsai, TFS,   subversion/ant, Mac Xcode, Clearcase/Clearquest, emacs/vi, Qt Creator, Microsoft Visual Studio.
Web: HTML (4/5), Javascript, CSS.   JQuery, learning Node.js.
Operating systems: Linux (RedHat, SuSE), Mac OS/X, Solaris, HP/UX, AIX. Some SuSE Linux, Windows.

positions.title: R&D Software Engineer
positions.description: Keysight has split off from Agilent; otherwise the information from my Agilent entry still applies.

positions.title: R&D Software Engineer
positions.description: Came from the acquisition of Xpedion Design Systems, where I was employed 2002-2006.   Configured, purchased, and run a small compute cluster for field use to respond to significant needs. Run team to develop new data storage mechanism for core applications. Responsible for our build/release flow and significant work on the design kit validator mentioned in the Xpedion entry below.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Supporting engineer to some of the smartest people I've ever known.   I don't hold it against them that they all have PhD's either.  We build one of the best RFIC circuit simulators in the world.  I build the parts which surround it: integrations with other tools and clustering software as well as a GUI-based design kit multi-simulator validation tool.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Mobile messaging company, moving messages between carriers and device types on the fly.    We even had, like, hardware in other countries!!!   At least for awhile,  until the money crowd gave up on us and had almost all of us fired (some of us twice, just to be sure) and sold Mobilesys to mBlox.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: I built supporting Infrastructure software (i.e., glueware) for the major applications and random interesting hobby projects used internally.   Won the occasional award from the sales force for helping them succeed.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Startup building the first VHDL simulator.   Acquired by Viewlogic, which became Innoveda (I think I was gone by then).  I worked on various aspects, including design/build of a schematic capture system linked to the patented (I even got on the patent) incremental design change technique.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Digital IC layout software.   Fun times for awhile; drum kits in the cubicles, testing chairs by bouncing them as high as we could, etc.   Never forget the 300Mb, 31 head (!) disk crash which used up all replacement heads the manufacturer had on the West Coast... Fortran, Mortran, Pascal, C, assembler, oh my.
